# Siegecraft, mining and counter-mining (`siegecraft_mining`)

<!-- generated by scripts/build_techtree.py from techtree/core/military.yaml — do not edit -->

- Category: Warfare, security & deterrence (`military`)
- Deps: helped by gunpowder, surveying_triangulation, torsion_artillery_trebuchet, cannon_artillery, coal_mining
- Core idea: A siege is methodical work: cut the place off with a ring of entrenchments, push covered approaches forward, and open the wall by ram, battery or mine. The classical mine is a timbered gallery dug under the foundation; the props are burnt and the wall falls. With gunpowder, a sealed chamber under the wall is packed with barrels and the gallery behind it blocked solid so that the blast goes upwards. The defender listens (a drum with dried peas or a bowl of water shows the vibration of digging), digs counter-galleries to break in, and fights, floods or smokes the miners out. Against bastions the attacker zigzags trenches forward so that they cannot be raked, joined by parallel trenches that hold troops and batteries (Vauban).
- Pitfalls:
  - A gallery driven straight at the wall without survey ends short or in the ditch; direction and distance must be measured
  - A powder chamber that is not tamped blows back down the gallery and kills the miners
  - Mines flood below the water table and suffocate their diggers without ventilation
  - Forgetting the outer line against a relief army; the Ottomans at Vienna in 1683 did not fortify their rear and were routed
  - Time decides: disease, hunger and the season usually threaten the besieger as much as the besieged
- History: mesopotamia: 9th–7th c. BC – Assyrian reliefs show rams, ramps, sappers and scaling (Lachish 701 BC); china: c. 4th c. BC – Mozi's siege chapters describe counter-mines, listening jars sunk in wells and bellows pumping smoke into enemy tunnels; greece: c. 350 BC – Aeneas Tacticus on detecting mines with a bronze shield; 305 BC – siege of Rhodes; rome: 52 BC – Caesar's ramp at Avaricum and circumvallation at Alesia; 49 BC – mines and counter-mines at Massilia; AD 256 – mine and counter-mine preserved at Dura-Europos; europe: 1487 – gunpowder mine tried at Sarzanello with little effect; 1495 – mine at Castel Nuovo, Naples (Francesco di Giorgio), often called the first effective one; 1503 – Pedro Navarro at Castel dell'Ovo; 1673 – Vauban's parallels at Maastricht; islamic: 1453 – Ottoman mines at Constantinople defeated by counter-mines; 1648–1669 – Candia, the school of Ottoman miners; 1683 – Vienna, 14 July to 12 September, mines wreck the ravelin and the Burg and Löbel bastions while the garrison counter-mines until the relief army arrives; india: 1567–1568 – Akbar's covered approaches and powder mines at Chittor
- Read:
  - Christopher Duffy, Siege Warfare: The Fortress in the Early Modern World 1494–1660 (1979)
  - John Stoye, The Siege of Vienna (1964)
  - Caesar, De bello Gallico VII
